utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that there were no preliminaries. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There are none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. Could I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by Ms. Hochhauser. You will find her to your right, Witness. And Ms. Hochhauser is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Hochhauser, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Tarcin. Can you please tell the Chamber your full name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I am Fadila Tarcin. I was born on the 19th of February, 1986 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, Ms. Tarcin, where is it that you're currently living?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I do apologise. I think you have a mistake here. The year of my birth is not 1986 but it's 1976. So it's 7-6.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I see that that is correct. In the running transcript that we have it was recorded as 1986, so that's now been corrected. Can you tell the Court, please, where you're living and if you're currently employed?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I currently live in Sarajevo, Berkusa Mala 24a is my address and I'm employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Ms. Tarcin, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor here at the ICTY on the 24th of February, 2004, and a second statement clarifying the first and providing some additional information on the 2nd of November, 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could, I would ask that 65 ter number 28440, which is the statement dated 24 February 2004, be placed on the monitor in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, ma'am, do you recognise the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could turn, please, in the English version to page 5 in e-court which I believe is the second-to-last page. Can you tell us, do you recognise the signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes. If you mean my signature, yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, this statement from 2004, did you have the opportunity over this past weekend to review a translation of this statement in your own language, in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And after reviewing it, were there any changes or corrections that you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, the statement is correct and everything I said is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So if you were asked the same questions today that you were asked when you provided the information that's contained in this statement, would the answers be the same today as it was when you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, they would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, if I could ask, please, for 65 ter number 28441, which is a statement dated 2nd November, 2008, be placed on the monitor. And, ma'am, do you recognise this document that's now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us -- if we could also turn in the English version again to the last -- to page 4 in e-court in the English version. And, again, do you recognise the signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Again, did you have the opportunity prior to testifying today to review a translation of this statement in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is there anything after reviewing it that you wanted to change or correct?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, there's nothing. I've read the statement and everything that is contained there is what I would say today as well, so there's nothing to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration testifying before this Chamber, can you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of both of those statements?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would tender 65 ter numbers 28440 and 28441 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28440 becomes Exhibit P281, Your Honours. And document 28441 becomes Exhibit P282, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P821 and P28 -- I made a mistake. P281 and P282 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honours, if I might read a brief summary what is now in evidence from Ms. Tarcin. Fadila Tarcin's testimony is relevant to schedule G as incident G1. On 28 May 1992, 16-year-old Fadila Tarcin lived with her family in the residential Sirokaca area of Sarajevo. On the evening of 28 May 1992 her residential neighbourhood came under intense shelling and the witness and her family moved to their cellar for protection. Sometime after midnight that night, the witness was sitting next to the cellar door when there was an explosion and the witness discovered that both of her legs were seriously injured. Due to the intensity of the shelling, Ms. Tarcin was unable to seek immediate medical attention but eventually made it to the hospital. Ms. Tarcin suffers long-term physical effects from her injuries, and the shelling that wounded her also extensively damaged residential houses in the immediate area of her home. Ms. Tarcin recalls in her written evidence hearing a radio broadcast sometime after her wounding on 28 May 1992, concerning an intercepted radio conversation featuring General Mladic in which he was directing the targeting of that shelling. That concludes the summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Tarcin, as I've said, I only really have about two very brief questions for you because the Chamber is in possession of your written evidence and has carefully examined it. First, in the statement that's now in evidence as Exhibit P281, which is your 2004 statement, at paragraph 2 you say that yours was a residential neighbourhood, the neighbourhood you and your family lived in. Can you tell us what the ethnic make-up of that neighbourhood was on 28 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: The population was predominantly Bosniak; that is to say Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Also, in both of your previous statements which are, again, in evidence you detailed as of those dates, as of the dates of those statements, the continuing effects of the injuries that you suffered on 28th of May, 1992. Can you tell the Chamber whether you still suffer consequences of that injury?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In all likelihood, these consequences will never go away. I was seriously wounded and one organ was permanently destroyed and that is a knuckle on my toe. And over the years it can only become more complicated. I do not walk properly. My spine is curved and increasingly so, so things get only worse.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Ma'am, my final question for you is: You reference in your statement hearing a radio broadcast of intercepted conversations with General Mladic. Can you tell us, tell the Chamber, whether you know exactly when it was in relation to your injury that you heard that broadcast?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly when this happened, when I first heard that broadcast. I don't know whether it was five, ten, or 15 days after I was injured. I cannot say exactly. You know, those were very difficult circumstances. For five days you'd have electricity and then you could hear something, and then you would not have any electricity and then you couldn't hear anything. And then you'd have electricity again for another two hours. So, quite simply, you lose all sense of time, whether five, ten, or 15 days had elapsed. So I cannot tell you exactly how much time had gone by after I had heard that broadcast for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said, it was -- I only had a few questions for Ms. Tarcin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser. Ms. Tarcin, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. And if you only testified only very shortly, have answered only a few questions put to you by the Prosecution, of course the Chamber has read your statement so there's more than what you told us this morning. Mr. Ivetic will now cross-examine you. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, ma'am. I would first ask that you try to pay attention to my questions and try to ensure that the answer you give is the most focused answer possible for my questions, and that way we will get through this as quickly as possible. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, first I'd like to go into some background issues. Were any members of your family taking part in the fighting as members of any armed force at any time prior to the 28th or the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, not in the fighting. But I can say that at the time in different neighbourhoods there were guards unarmed, as a rule, and quite simply during the night they were on duty there in the street. If something unexpected happened, then they could inform other people, but at that point in time they were not [Realtime transcript read in error "in the"] armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time, as a 16-year-old girl, have any knowledge of the front lines; that is to say, where the warring forces were located and fighting with one another?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I did not know then where the lines were exactly. We knew that the area where I -- I mean, the area where I live is hilly, so we knew that the fighting was taking place above our houses, or rather, that the lines were above our houses, but I didn't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the time-period prior to 28/29 May 1992, did you have occasion to ever eye-witness or see the front line positions so as to know their location?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When the fighting started, did you have a chance to go outside and walk around the neighbourhood of Sirokaca or did you primarily stay at home, indoors?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I stayed at home most of the time, and if I went out it was only within 200 or 300 metres around the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the weeks leading up to 28/29 May 1992, did you have occasion to go to school or had classes been interrupted by the situation?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I didn't go to school. Schools were not working; they stopped already in April. So in that period of time, we did not go to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've identified for us that if you did go out you usually only stayed approximately 200 metres or 300 metres around the house. Could you please tell us, using any type of measurement or parameter that you can, approximately how expansive is the entire neighbourhood of Sirokaca; that is to say, how big is it geographically?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly in terms of kilometres. The area that we call Sirokaca is not an administrative unit. There is, actually, an administrative unit of Sirokaca, but it basically denotes a broader area, broader than the administrative unit, that is. It is possible that the diameter is 2 or 3 kilometres, but I wouldn't be able to say that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Did you ever have a chance to venture outside of Sirokaca to go to other parts such as Bistrik or Stari Grad in May of 1992 or the weeks prior to May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that within 2- or 300 metres, the areas you're referring to, because the witness said she never went out any further than 2- or 300 metres. Now, if Bistrik or Stari Grad is within 2- or 300 metres --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to find out, Your Honour, which part of Sirokaca she's at. I don't know myself. Personally, I've never been to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where have you never been?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you know on a map where it is, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes. I understand that Bistrik is right there, but you could have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that within 2- or 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know. They are adjoining areas. So it's possible that a person could be 200 metres from the neighbouring area, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Bistrik or Stari Grad? And I'll check it on the map, Mr. -- Witness, could you tell us whether in those weeks just before the event, whether you ever went to Bistrik or Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the occasions when you walked around 200 to 300 metres around your home, did you ever have occasion to eye-witness any armed formations of the Territorial Defence, the army, or the police situated or patrolling in Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Maybe once or twice I had an opportunity to see the reserve police that just passed through the area. I would not say that it's a formation. It would be three to four men, never more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And apart from your own observations of occasionally one or two times seeing three to four reserve policemen, did you have occasion to hear from other people about the existence of any Territorial Defence, army, or police forces that were situated in or patrolling Sirokaca prior to the date that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Yes, my neighbours were saying that there is a Territorial Defence, that there is a reserve police, but no one said where they were or how many of them there were. No one mentioned any specific figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could tell me after you left the hospital, did you and your family remain living in the same Sirokaca neighbourhood or did you move elsewhere for the remainder of the war?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, we lived in the same house throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to focus on the time-period after you returned to your home from the hospital, that is to say from June 1992 through 1995, did you at any time become aware of any armed forces of the so-called Armija of BiH being based in Sirokaca or passing through Sirokaca to battle with the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not based there; but as for whether they passed through or not, I really can't tell. I can only assume that it was possible that they did, but I myself never saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough, ma'am. Did you have occasion to ever see or hear about any artillery forces of the Army of BiH being positioned in or near Sirokaca in that time-period, again after you were treated and released from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Specifically in Sirokaca I didn't hear anything about that and I definitely never saw anything to that effect, and I never heard that there was any artillery weaponry positioned in Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you some questions about parts of the statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. First, I would like to look at P281, which is your statement dated the 24th of February, 2004, and I'd like to ask you about paragraph 2 of the same which is on page 2 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S in e-court. And I believe it's up on the screen. Madam, there you identify that the only military establishment near to your home was the barracks some 1.5 kilometres away at Bistrik. For the record, can you tell us what force occupied these barracks; that is to say in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think that until May this barracks were occupied by the JNA; however, I don't know exactly when they left it. It might even have been as early as in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough. And after they left, were these barracks occupied by someone else or were they empty, if you know?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I don't have any exact knowledge at to who went there and when it happened exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. If I can now ask to direct your attention to paragraph 11 of this statement. This is on the third page in English and the fourth page in B/C/S. And we earlier talked about the front lines and you answered as you answered, so now I want to ask you: Here in paragraph 11 you indicate at the end of the paragraph: "We were also at least a kilometre from the front lines." Could you explain that answer for me in light of what you said today about your knowledge of the front lines. Is this an estimate on your part? Or did you definitely know which front line is referenced here?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, and in my statement I just expressed my opinion. Therefore, I don't know exactly. As I said, those were edges of the area which means that the lines were above our houses. However, how many kilometres away they were, I don't know. My estimate was that it was 1 to 2 kilometres, but I really cannot tell you the exact distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "above our houses," were the front lines between Bistrik and Sirokaca or between Sirokaca and another suburb or area?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Bistrik is located below Sirokaca, which means that the lines were not between Bistrik and Sirokaca but rather above Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up for me. As I indicated, I have not had the opportunity to visit Sirokaca so it's unclear to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you can see it on the map. It's quite clear that Bistrik is further down and Sirokaca is further up the hill and then it goes further up and that's where the -- at least on maps we find front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and her answer of "above our houses" needs to be cleared up and that's why I asked them the way I did without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then you asked whether it was further down as you can see on the map, because there are indications there on what goes uphill and what goes -- there are altitude lines so it's just a question which doesn't make sense. And usually rivers are further down. Miljacka river is further down in the direction of Bistrik. Please try to deal with the information available as intelligently as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Madam, while we're still on paragraph 11 I'd like to ask you about the other words that are recorded there, including: "... there were no troop concentrations, military positions, or other such places that could have been construed as military targets." Are all of these your words or were they words that were suggested to you by perhaps the person interviewing you, in particular "construed as a military target"?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: These are my words and my opinion. I don't know how familiar you are with Sarajevo and how these neighbourhood look like. You have small family houses which are clustered together next to one another with almost no gap between them. Therefore, I don't know what major troop concentration there could exist. All these houses were varying between one-storey to three-storey houses. In a word, those were regular family homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you can only know what you saw or heard about in regards to troop concentrations or military positions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm going to object to that question. I'm not sure what it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think what Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: What it's asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ivetic is asking: Can you only see what you see, can you only know what you've either seen or heard. That's your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is the -- is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you think it would assist the Chamber in itself to have these kind of general statements? You can only see something if you don't have your eyes closed, isn't it, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm trying to see for paragraph 11 what the basis of that was -- if it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If it was beyond her own knowledge. That is what I'm trying to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do that directly then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam witness, with respect to paragraph 11, are the conclusions stated therein based on your own personal observations and what you heard or on other sources?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Partly it is based on what I saw because I had an opportunity to see it, but as much as I was able to see I didn't see any concentration of military troops. I never heard anyone speaking about concentration of major military forces. Therefore, that's what it is based upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have twice now used the term "major military forces." I'm asking about forces in general. Would your answer be the same with regard to forces in general as opposed to major military forces?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I may have misspoken. I was referring to any military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now, since we're at this page, I'd like to ask you about paragraph 12 which regards the broadcast on the radio that you heard that you believe was General Mladic giving directions. First of all, am I correct that the locations that you heard from this radio broadcast, none of them were the location of Sirokaca where you were injured on the 28th of May -- 28th/29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was no mention of Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from the fact that the radio identified the voice as that of General Mladic, did you have any independent knowledge yourself to permit you to identify that voice as belonging to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I'm not an expert of any sort. I cannot tell you, therefore, exactly whether that was his voice or not, but I established a connection between this voice and some later statements made by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that. With regard to those later statements, how many later statements are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact number. If I heard something in relation to Srebrenica, I cannot tell you exactly how many times it was mentioned because I didn't keep any record of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now I'd like to show you a document. It's already in evidence as Exhibit D39, and this is an intercept of a conversation between General Mladic and another individual dated 29 May 1992. And I would like to turn to page 5 in e-court in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S. Again, page 4 in the B/C/S and page 5 in the English version. And, madam, in the B/C/S it's the part spoken by Mr. Mladic towards the last half of the page, near the middle but not quite in the middle. And I will read for you the English so that you can locate it. And, again, this is reported to be Ratko Mladic saying as follows: "I agree. I want the same thing. If they want peace, they can have it. I ordered yesterday evening as soon as I arrived, there was that attack not only against the units but also against you. This shooting, somehow I managed to calm down the men here, to get them under control, to stop them from firing. This thing they are doing now, they probably have good pantomimes or good impressionists who probably successfully imitated our voices, mine, yours, everybody's." Madam, did you happen to know of any such possibility of people imitating the voices of General Mladic prior to today?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, to the extent you want to draw the attention of the Chamber to the basis on which the witness testified that what she heard on the radio - whether that was Mr. Mladic's voice, yes or no - that point is perfectly clear to us now. The witness, as far as we understand, had no personal knowledge of Mr. -- she never met Mr. Mladic. If you refer to other statements given by Mr. Mladic then of course we could explore to what extent those were authentic or not. We could deal with that for another two or three hours. The point you want to make is perfectly clear to the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now turn to your other statement briefly, and that is, I believe, P282 which is dated the 2nd of November, 2008, and I have just a few brief questions about this relating, I think, to only one paragraph. And I think it is the second page in English and the second page in the B/C/S. And it is paragraph 3. And now we have that on the screen, madam. First of all, can you confirm whether or not the incident wherein you were wounded was reported to the local police?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: As far as I know, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would it be accurate to say that no one, in fact, be it police, army, or any international bodies, performed an investigation of the shelling site where you were injured?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Not that I know of and, as I said in my statement, that was not common procedure because there were so many shells falling down, which leads me to believe that it would have been difficult to achieve.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I understand your general answer, but I have to ask about specific items. Did anyone take any measurements or pictures of the scene, either at the time or at any time thereafter?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did anyone preserve any of these shell fragments or casings?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you mention men in the neighbourhood saying that it was "large-calibre howitzer shell." Am I correct that we're talking just about regular civilians or are we talking about anyone with specific knowledge of these things?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, these were civilians who had previously served in the JNA, just like the majority of men in our country did; and on that basis they were able to form some opinions of theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: But I cannot say that they were experts, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, and I appreciate that. Now, in this paragraph you also state: "According to the locals, the shell came from Borije to the east of us." First of all, are these locals the same neighbours that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this site that they had mentioned, Borije, could you tell us how far away Borije is from that location, from the site where you were injured?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I really have no idea. One can see them, but I really have no clue as to how many kilometres was the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about in relation to the front lines? Where would Borije be situated in regard to the front lines you earlier indicated as being somewhere located above your houses?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Opposite of us, due east. If you view it from Sirokaca, it would be opposite, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct that this area of Borije was held mainly by the forces loyal to the Izetbegovic government?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I honestly don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. I'd like to then move to another topic. First of all, are you familiar with the area of Sirokaca where there is a primary school located?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I attended that primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, since I'm not from Sirokaca, is there only one primary school in Sirokaca or are there multiple primary schools within that neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: There's only one in Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how far is that one primary school from the place where your home was located in Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I can only suppose that it was 3- to 400 metres as the crow flies, but I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge or did you hear that that particular school during 1992, 1993, and 1994 was used by the army of the BiH forces to billet their soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about that, therefore I cannot say either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify since you said it's about 3- to 400 metres as the crow flies, did you have occasion to visit the school during the time-periods when you were walking around your house, 200 to 300 metres around your house, in the time-period of May 1992 or the weeks prior?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if the school is about 400 metres as the crow flies and I walk only up to 300 metres, how do I get to the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Because she said 300 to 400 metres, Your Honours. I'm trying to clarify to see if it's more 400 or 300 if she would have had an occasion to see the school on the occasions that she travelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, perhaps I can simplify the question: Did you ever have occasion to get a glimpse of the school during the time-period when you would have walked 200 to 300 metres around your house?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I didn't have such occasion. Well, speaking about walking within the radius of 2- to 300 metres, I'm not talking about a stroll but rather about the area that we had a chance to find some water springs. In other words, the walk involved going to fetch water if you didn't have it on the specific day. That was not a recreational walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, madam, and I did not mean to imply otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we're at the time for the break and I have another approximately 30 to 35 minutes and I would be moving on to a different topic, so it would be a convenient time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would be a convenient time for the break. We will take the break after the witness has left the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in approximately 20 minutes and then we'll continue for as Mr. Ivetic indicated approximately another half an hour. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Ivetic, could you tell us where apparently you are linking a school with a military object? Could you tell us where that school is in Sirokaca? There seems to be only one and I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's why I asked if there was only one. It was discussed in the Galic trial with another witness who was from the same region and that's where the information I have comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not investigated where that school is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so it all remains vague and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, it's for me to track it down and bring Defence evidence then if that, in fact, is proven true to demonstrate. All I know is there is one primary school in Sirokaca and that in the Galic proceedings there was some evidence that there were forces billeted there. This witness said she had no knowledge of that so I don't think I can explore further with this witness that. I don't have any documents to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but where that is, that is within 500 metres from her house or 700 metres from her house -- I mean, a witness of course is usually not very good at assessing distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see what you mean to say. It's an objective distances. No, I do not have that, Your Honours. I could -- I think I should investigate that and find some objective standard to present to Your Honours, either through another witness or from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We take a break and resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber would have a few questions for the witness. Could we have P3 on our screen, page 76 in e-court. Could we zoom in on the further to the right top corner of this, even a bit more on the word "Sirokaca." Yes. Witness, can you see on the map, can you orient yourself? I see that the Berkusa Mala seems to be indicated just above the word "Bostarici." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that the street where you used to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be able to mark on this map the exact place of your house, orienting yourself to the other names of the streets and I think at the top you see the road that goes through from east to west. Do you see that? I think it had a specific -- has a specific name or hasn't it? You see that on the top? Perhaps we could slightly move out and go a little bit. Wait with marking until you get instructions. Are you better able now to orient yourself? You still see Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, now it's better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we zoom in again on Sirokaca and especially on the street I just referred to, would you be able to mark on this map where your house was? The usher will give you a ... What happens? Could we have the same ... Mr. Usher, could you assist the witness in using the right equipment. Take your time to orient yourself again. If you mark it with a letter K, which would stand for Kuca I think for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now on this map are you able to find the street where the school was? If you would like to have it zoomed in more or zoomed out more, please tell us and we'll do as you indicate. Yes, we'll not zoom in and out because then we lose the marking, but are you able to find the street where the school was and the approximate location of the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could zoom in once again. This way it's difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have to re-mark later the K because it will be lost. But we know where it is, it's just to the M of Mala, the name of your street. Could we zoom in again. Perhaps you repeat your marking of your own house with a K, which was just at Berkusa Mala just near to the M.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, maybe last time I marked too high. It's closer to this intersection we see on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please correct it as you consider accurate. If you want to change it, the usher can help you to remove whatever you want to change. Because if you said it was too high, it's now even a bit higher than you did it for the first time, I think. Could we remove the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, it's not all right, not even now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take it out. Mr. Usher, could you -- yes, so it's wiped out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we erase this too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand your marking is now a bit further down the street compared to the first one, a little bit closer to the centre of Sirokaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, the house is in the street itself on the line marking the street, and you enter the house from the street. So it's not removed from the centre of the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was not talking about the centre of the street but the centre of the settlement of Sirokaca. But you have now marked the house. Could you mark the place, to the extent you're able to do so, where the school was? And if you do it with the S of Skola, then ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm able to tell on the map, I think it was there -- it is still there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could this receive a Chamber exhibit number. It would be, Madam Registrar ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be C1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. C1 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to take a look at 65 ter number 1D00318, which is a statement dated the 25th of March, 1996, of Sl Sljivo Jasmin, a member of the BH army. First of all, we will not be seeking to admit this statement through the witness, but portions are relevant in relation to the neighbourhood of Sirokaca and I'd like to see if the witness has any knowledge or if it assists us in getting to the truth of the matter. At this time I think we need to go to the fifth page in English and also the fifth page of the B/C/S in this document. And the portion that I would like to direct the attention to would be immediately under the heading of "amendment to the statement." And, Ms. Witness, if I can direct your attention to the portion that begins as follows: "As a member of the Muslim people, immediately after the SDA was formed I joined it. At the beginning of January 1991 at one of the SDA meetings in the Cultural Centre at Sirokaca I heard from Faik Avdibegovic for the Green Berets as a military formation of the SDA. On that occasion we were told that the commander of the Green Berets in BH was Svrakic Emin and Avdibegovic Faik was appointed for the area of Sirokaca. About 200 people at the very beginning joined the military formation of the Green Berets of Sirokaca. The code for Fadil Avdibegovic and our unit was 'Bosna 27.' At the very beginning of January 1991, Emin Svrakic sent 70 A rifles to our unit, which were immediately distributed by Faik at his own discretion. On that occasion Faik issued the order for us to organise ourselves and to control the terrain from Sirokaca to the hotel 'Osmice' by patrols." First of all, ma'am, did you happen to hear or know of a Mr. Faik Avdibegovic being in Sirokaca either in 1991 or after the war started?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: The name Faik Avdibegovic is familiar, but I don't know the man personally. I don't know where he was in the period you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say that the name is familiar. Is it familiar to you in the context of him being the commander of a group of 200 persons in Sirokaca or in some other context?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I know the name as a name I have heard, not in the context of his being a commander, not in that sense. I just heard the name but not in the context you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough. Are you familiar with the cultural centre and did you have occasion to hear of any meetings of any military formations in the culture centre in 1991?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I know where the cultural centre was, but I never heard of any meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- are you surprised to learn of the alleged existence of a 200-person-strong unit controlling the terrain from Sirokaca to the Osmice hotel, as alleged by this document?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether the witness was surprised or not, Mr. Ivetic, do you really think it would assist the Chamber? You could ask her whether she had any knowledge. Because surprise is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you have a different impression, isn't it? So if you ask about it and I think until now the witness said she didn't say anything -- she didn't know anything -- she never observed any troops, apart from this was all 1991, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge of any troops organising patrols in Sirokaca, controlling the terrain from the Osmice hotel to Sirokaca in 1991?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you help us again with the geography. Where is this terrain, this Osmice hotel? Where would it be situated in relation to Sirokaca and in relation to your home? And if you think you would be assisted by the map, we could go to the map.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Maybe it would be clearer to you if I showed it on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you: Was it further away from your home than the school was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Considerably further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you really in any unit of measurement, but the school is approximately at the same level as my house, whereas Osmice hotel is above my house, above the entire neighbourhood of Sirokaca in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean higher up the hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- proceed as you wish, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have P3 and I believe it was page 76 in the same map that we just had up on the screen before. And if we could perhaps again zoom generally in the area where the words "Sirokaca" are displayed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with the assistance of the usher, madam, I would ask, perhaps in some colour that would be distinguishable from the text that's on the map, when the usher gets there, if you could identify for us generally the location of the hotel. I understand that you perhaps cannot be precise with this map and this equipment, but the general location of the hotel that is mentioned in this document, the Osmice hotel.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a bit on the map because this way I can't see the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If possible, can we zoom in for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps a little bit further down because the witness said it was higher up the hill. A little bit more, a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this position of the map helpful, Madam Witness, to identify the approximate location of the Osmice hotel?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No. I think the hotel is still further above, that means lower on the map. A bit further to my left. No, the other way, the other way, my left. This is really difficult for me. I can only suppose where it was, but I can't mark it exactly on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. If you could perhaps describe for us in reference to either the -- any of the other printed text on the map where the general area is, that should suffice I think.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: That should be in the area of Brajkovac probably. I really cannot say for sure now. I cannot tell on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I see that the witness has indicated somewhere near the bottom of the map where -- Brajkovac is in the bottom portion of the map we now have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two Brajkovacs, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise if there's two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is one in the real bottom but a little bit further -- higher up to the left there is another Brajkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, when you say "Brajkovac," do you mean the one that is near to Lipe or the one that's near to Cicin Han, for the same of clarity?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Lipe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could return to the previous document which was again 1D00318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if it is the Brajkovac near Lipe, could you agree with the Prosecution that the distance to the house is anywhere between 400 and 450 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of that location, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you need two to agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Judge, I would have to just take a closer look but I'll come back prepared to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's just using the scale on the bottom of the map and looking at the map and what the distance is, isn't it? If you take the original one, sheet 11, and then take a small pice of paper, mark the distance and then match it with the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, you have the advantage on me because I didn't have the actual map book out so I can't see the scale as listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. On my little piece of paper we are coming close to 500 metres, please proceed. But please let me know at a later stage whether there is any agreement with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say, because it seems to be relevant now, that the Prosecution does have a computer software that has a capacity to get very, very precise measurements between locations, and perhaps the better way to proceed is that any location or distance that the Chamber feels is important to the trial, we'll sit down with the Defence at that software, review it, and I think we'll be able to more confidently agree to distances once we've both had the benefit of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Groome, I take it that Mr. Ivetic will respond to this invitation, but it certainly would have saved a lot of time in court if Mr. Ivetic would have oriented himself on the locations which were already known to him; that is, the school and this centre. I mean, must be able to find out where approximately it is and see how relevant it is. So I'm not saying this moment having the impression, a provisional impression, that the distance to the place mentioned by Mr. Ivetic is approximately 4- to 500 metres -- so the relevance is for Mr. Ivetic to consider. And we'll then of course think about it. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could return to -- oh, we're already there. If we could turn to I believe it is page 6 in both languages. I'll just verify that. Yes, it's 6 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The previous document you used, do you intend to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is the same document, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the part I want is beginning on the second paragraph of the page in English and also in the B/C/S and it starts as follows, beginning quote: "After the training was completed we took the oath and, as far as I can remember, it consisted of the following words: 'I will swear that I will defend BH with all my heart and especially Sarajevo from the Serbs and Croats.' After that we said 'alah uegber' three times. "After the return to Sarajevo we were tasked by Faik to patrol with weapons through Sirokaca and to establish check-points. We carried out those activities from some time in March 1991 until April 1992." End of the selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, do you have any knowledge or recollection of check-points being armed -- being set up by armed men in existence in Sirokaca from 1991 March until April 1992, as described in this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I might just object to the manner in which these -- this questioning is proceeding with the reading of passages from this document that don't ultimately reflect the point of the question, which is: Does the witness have knowledge of check-points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: It's preceded by a lengthy recitation of information that the witness couldn't possibly have knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do not know. Do you have any knowledge of check-points in the area between March 1991 and April 1992, in Sirokaca of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw any such check-points and no one ever told me that they saw something like this. I must say that I really am surprised now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness never saw anything of the kind apparently. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I move on. Again, I will not be seeking to admit this document at this time through this witness. I would like to now take a look at another document that's been marked as 1D00317 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you also again first explore with the witness whether she has any knowledge about the matter you later will show to her in this document. I don't know what it is about --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you just ask her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of artillery located in Sirokaca being used to strike at Vraca and Serb positions in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 1D00317.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we wait for that, madam, for your information this is an intercept that was disclosed by the Office of the Prosecutor purporting to be dated the 22nd of April, 1992, and it is between -- it claims to be between Radovan Karadzic and a man named Momo. Again, we will not be seeking to introduce this through this witness but believes that it deals with matters relevant to the witness's testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you first ask the witness whether there's anything -- you may have a subject on your mind you want to ask questions about, whether she knows anything about what you want to touch upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, I just asked if there was shelling in April of 1992 from Sirokaca on Vraca and this is what this intercept deals with, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Do you have any knowledge about shelling from Sirokaca to Vraca in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we first look at page 2 of this document in the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could look there, madam, there's a section where they're talking about 50 to 60 shells falling on the territory of Vraca and it's -- the inference is that those are coming from Zlatiste. Could you tell us where Zlatiste is located in relation to Sirokaca and the neighbourhood where your home is.

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: Zlatiste, well it's an area like Osmice and Brajkovac, on the outskirts. We've already seen all of that on the map. It's above Sirokaca. So that line that you are talking about and is Brajkovac-Osmice-Zlatiste. That's on the outskirts. Now, what the actual distance is, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's okay. There's a specific part of the document where Momo begins --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first ask: What is Zlatiste? Is that a hill or is it a village or is it a river? What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the most accurate thing we can say is that it's a hill. There were a few houses at Zlatiste, but not enough to call it a settlement. I mean, I don't know how many houses there were there, but it wasn't a big settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, we see Zlatiste on sheet 11. Is that what you're exploring?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was exploring the locations that are identified in this intercept, Your Honours, yes. So Zlatiste being one, the other being Vraca. I'd like to ask about Vraca, where Vraca is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, any effort made to agree with the Prosecution where Zlatiste and where Vraca is? I mean, if you start asking a witness where Paris is, I would suggest that you first ask whether you can agree with the Prosecution where Paris is, that's the same for London and could be for Zlatiste and Vraca as well. I mean, this witness is called for other reasons, I think. And, of course, if you would be a great geographer, and if it's close to her house I can imagine that you use the testimony of such a witness. If it is further away from the house. But she said Zlatiste, but we see it on the map. Now, if that is what the witness intended to say, she said it was further from Brajkovac. I, by the way, now see that there are three Brajkovacs on the map. Proceed as you wish, but try to find the most efficient way of establishing facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me skip right to the middle of the page then of this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if we're talking about Vraca, is that Vraca or -- because I see Vraca on the map which is -- well, at least some few kilometres away from where the witness said she lived, I think, as the crow flies, 3 kilometres. Is that the Vraca you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's a Vraca identified in this intercept and I believe it is that one, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So how could the witness know which Vraca they refer to? So I take it you have formed an opinion about whether that is the Vraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, would you agree with the Prosecution that Vraca is on this same sheet 11, approximately 1 kilometre from the left of the margin of the map, close -- if that's what you think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, Judge, I can't agree that that's the Vraca that's being referred to in this intercept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- but I can agree that there's a Vraca that's indicated on the map close to the left-hand border such as you've indicated. And I would also in response to your earlier question of whether there's been any effort to agree, we would agree that all of these neighbourhoods as depicted on the map are such as they are on the map in terms of their relationship to one another, that this is the correct geographical layout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention, again it's the middle of the page of this document where it starts "half an hour ago." And if you read those -- it's at the top -- I'm sorry, it's right there at the top of the page in the B/C/S, middle of the page in the English. If you read the next one, two, three, four, five, six -- 15 or so lines, they're talking about artillery fire and artillery pieces located at Sirokaca. And the original name Momo is reported as saying: "At Sirokaca. And as for the urban part, most probably down there from the 'Zeljeznicar' stadium." From the Zeljeznicar stadium. "Yes, yes." Are these -- is that an area that is familiar to you as being near Sirokaca -- the Sirokaca neighbourhood where you lived; and if not, where is it located?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: I am a bit confused because here it says Sirokaca and the Zeljeznicar stadium. So I don't understand. What does the question actually refer to, which part? Both Sirokaca and the Zeljeznicar stadium are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about Sirokaca as a site that was identified in addition to the Zeljeznicar stadium. Is there only one area known as Sirokaca in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: As far as I know, there's only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know where the Zeljeznicar stadium is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us where it approximately is. Is it near to your house? Is it in Sirokaca? Or is it elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not nearby. It's the area of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could take the time to look at 1D00315. This document, madam, you'll see is a combat report of Commander Sipcic of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS, and it is dated 19 June 1992, just a few weeks after you were wounded. And if we can look at item 1 of this report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, again, first explore with the witness whether she has any knowledge about the matter that you want to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do -- madam, now I know that you were probably recovering from your wounds, but did you have occasion in the weeks following your wounding to have any knowledge of any attacks conducted by Bosnian Muslim forces originating from Sirokaca and being directed at surrounding areas, including towards the -- originating from Sirokaca towards Zlatiste?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect -- with respect to item 1 we see here that the document purports to state that the enemy used mortar fire. Are you familiar or did you have occasion to hear of mortars being either transported through Sirokaca or being stationed in Sirokaca in the weeks following, again in June 1992, following your release from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: No. After I was wounded, for at least six months I did not leave the basement. So really, all information from that period is very scant, I mean the information I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what about -- you say you were off for six months. And what about the period of October 1992 specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the Chamber wonders whether you want to go through the whole of the conflict, all of the -- everything that happened around Sirokaca. What is the relevance of that at this moment? And second, where the witness has told us again and again and again that she has no knowledge of military, that she hadn't seen them, et cetera, what would you expect to continue this line of questioning?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it goes towards the credibility and the reliability of the witness's testimony where she talks about there not being any military installations nearby or military concentrations nearby --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- and this shows that they were ongoing at every stage. There is military in and around Sirokaca is the Defence's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then the witness apparently has not seen that, has not observed that. Well, now being in the basement for most of the time, moving out of the house now and then for 2- or 300 metres would -- it might not surprise that she didn't see mortars passing through Sirokaca, if there were any at any point in time. It seems that what you're asking the witness doesn't bring much what would assist the Chamber at this moment. To the extent you have challenged any opinion about military presence, I think that point is clear and we don't have to go through all of the years of the conflict to further explore that with this witness. This witness testifies primarily on being wounded when her house, or at least the neighbouring house, was shelled on a certain date and what the effect of that attack to that area was. That is where the Chamber considers the importance, the primary importance, of this witness to be. You have explored a few other things, not to much avail, because the witness just doesn't know. And you should not continue that unless there's any specific matter where you could have a reasonable expectation that the witness could tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, then I will heed Your Honour's instruction and will not ask about other reports of interactions between the military forces in this region.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at that point then, madam, I thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have touched all the topics that I wanted to with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give an opportunity to re-examine the witness, Ms. Hochhauser, I would have one question for you. I do understand from your statement that you were wounded by shrapnel when a neighbouring house was hit by a projectile. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, have you later seen the impact on that house of your neighbour's, the impact of that shell, if it did hit the house itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it hit the house itself and, yes, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us, was the impact on the side of the house facing the hill, uphill therefore; or was the impact from downhill? Or neither of the two, that's also a possibility.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was facing downhill, that is to say facing town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Facing town. Which means that the impact -- if I would take the house and look from the impact, that it would be rather the -- from the direction of the river, from the valley, rather than from uphill. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Hochhauser, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I only have one question which may, in fact, be more of a transcription error, but I'd like to clear it up while she's still here. And I would refer Your Honours to page 8 beginning at line 1 going through 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And I would just ask you, Witness, you were asked a question earlier where you said -- where the question was -- I'd like -- excuse me: "Were any members of your family taking part in the fighting as any members of any armed force at any time prior to the 28th or the 29th of May, 1992? And I'll -- I'm going to skip the first three lines of your answer, but the last line of your answer was -- the last line of your answer as recorded is: "If something unexpected happened, then they could inform other people, but at that point in time...," and you were referring to guards in the different neighbourhoods, "... at that point in time they were in the armed." Can you clarify whether your testimony was whether they were armed at that point in time or unarmed?

utterances.speaker: FADILA TARCIN
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said that they were unarmed. But it is possible that at that moment I misspoke. So they were not armed. The guards in my neighbourhood were not armed, at least those that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's my only question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions from the Defence. Ms. Tarcin, this concludes your evidence in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering the questions that were put to you by the Prosecution and by the Defence and by the Chamber. I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. May I take it that the Prosecution is ready to call its next witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Prosecution is ready to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while the witness is being brought in, Your Honour, we've reviewed the adjudicated facts related to Mr. Sejmenovic's testimony and we've made certain redactions in his 92 ter statement on the basis of facts 855, 972 through 74, 983 through 87, 1063, 1066, 1070, and 1071. I'd also note that a chart of clarifications to the statement has been prepared, which we provided directly to the Defence and Chamber by e-mail yesterday pursuant to the Chamber's instructions of last Friday. Finally, regarding 65 ter 22696, a video associated with Mr. Sejmenovic's statement, I'd just advise the Chamber that I will be tendering the video as an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sejmenovic, I take it. Mr. Sejmenovic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. It's handed out to you. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Sejmenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Mevludin Sejmenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, where did you live in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992 I lived in the village of Trnopolje, close to Kozarac, which is in Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you recall providing a statement to this Tribunal on 13 August of this year?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask the court officer to please display 65 ter 28437 on our screens. It's a statement by Mr. Sejmenovic signed on 13 August 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, now that the document is on the screen before you, I'd ask that you view this first page, in particular the signature at the bottom, and I'd ask you if you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's a document that I signed and the signature at the bottom of the document is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd ask that we turn now to page 14 of the English. And once that comes up, I'll ask you to indicate again whether you recognise the signature, this time at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. At the top of the page is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read and review this statement in preparation for your appearance here today?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: I have read my statement, and after reading and considering it I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did you read it again recently in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask the court officer to now please display 65 ter 28445, a document entitled: Clarifications to statement of RM094. Did you also review this document in preparation for your statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I read this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And does it accurately reflect clarifications to your statement which you made after reviewing that statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If the Chamber were to consider your statement in conjunction with these clarifications now before us, will they have an accurate record of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if I were today to ask you questions similar to those you were asked in the taking of this statement, would you give the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, having established the foundational requirements necessary, the Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 28437 and 28445 into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. 28437, Madam Registrar, receives number ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. 28445 receives number ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Becomes Exhibit P284, Your Honours.
